text:
Anya: Heads up — ap-south1 showing ~12% GPU capacity drop, racks rck-17/rck-18/rck-19. ECC soft errors and Xid 31/43 counts jumped in the last 10m. Prod inference tail latency spiked 2s+.
Sam: Oof. Any recent changes to firmware/drivers or network fabric in that zone?
Anya: No config pushes from infra in the last 24h. We did have a BGP flapping event from cloud-provider peering ~45m ago but it stabilized. Error patterns look correlated with kernel driver resets (dmesg xid entries).
Ciara: I'm on it. Kicking off a targeted probe across the three racks to get per-card ECC/Xid and recent mttr. Will paste output.
infra-bot: Alert: ECC_RATE_HIGH ap-south1 rck-17,rck-18,rck-19 — threshold breached ( > 5x baseline ). Incident ID: INC-AP-5421.
Ciara: Running probe:
```
fleet-probe --region=ap-south1 --racks=rck-17,rck-18,rck-19 --metrics=ecc,xid --since=30m --format=summary
--- SUMMARY ---
 rck-17: 12 GPUs degraded, avg_ecc_rate=0.67% (baseline 0.06%), xid_rate=0.14%
 rck-18: 9 GPUs degraded, avg_ecc_rate=0.59%, xid_rate=0.11%
 rck-19: 11 GPUs degraded, avg_ecc_rate=0.72%, xid_rate=0.16%
Top error IDs: Xid 31, Xid 43, soft ECC on bus 3
Last driver reloads: 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC (cluster-wide planned rollout)
```
Sam: Interesting — driver reload was a while ago but rollout was cluster-wide. Could be a latent interaction with kernel module + NIC driver + specific card batch. Do we see vendor serial clustering?
Ciara: Yes, serial ranges: SN-0A1B* concentrated in rck-17/19. I pulled hardware mapping.
Lee: Two immediate mitigation paths: 1) partial drain and reprovision from other regions (costly, but quick), or 2) soft-evict only offending cards (if runtime supports per-card pinning) and let scheduler avoid them. Any preference?
Mike: Cost note — moving capacity cross-region will push up egress and burst capacity spend. If we fall back to reserveds we can absorb load but monthly cost jumps. Suggest attempt scheduler avoidance + throttle low-priority jobs first.
Anya: Agreed. Ops: can we implement scheduler avoidance quickly? How invasive?
ops-oncall: We can tag GPU nodes as avoid-inference via node-label and bump priority for reserve pool. Risk: small routing gaps while pods remap ~1-3m.
Ciara: Doing a canary: marking rck-17 GPUs with node-label avoid-inference for low-latency routes and draining only low-prio pods. Executing now.
infra-bot: Action logged: node-label apply rck-17/* avoid-inference by Ciara at 2221003550.
Ciara: Canary result: 5% capacity recovered for ap-south1; tail latency back ~900ms (from +2s). ECC counts still elevated on affected cards but user-visible impact reduced.
Sam: Good. We need root cause — propose grabbing NVML logs and driver klogs from a couple of the most-affected GPUs and coordinate with vendor. Also consider rolling back to previous kernel/driver image for a single rack as a canary.
Lee: I can prep an image rollback playbook. Rollback risk: if it doesn't help, we lose time and possibly destabilize other racks. But we can do rack-sized canary at 02:00 UTC with strict rollback cutover.
Mike: Also think about provisioned replacements — order margin GPUs? Procurement timeline is weeks; not helpful for immediate. Short term: use burst capacity in eu-west/na while we stabilize. Estimate extra cost of $8k/day if we shift 15% workload.
Anya: Ok decision: 1) Continue scheduler avoidance and low-prio eviction now (Ciara). 2) Gather logs and open vendor ticket (Sam+Ciara). 3) Run a rollback canary on rck-18 at 02:00 UTC (Lee to execute, Sam to monitor), escalation path if rollback fails is full drain of rck-18. 4) If more than 10% persistent capacity loss after canary, trigger cross-region burst allocation and notify finance (Mike).
Ciara: Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/incidents/INC-AP-5421/ — bundle name: ap5421-logs-2221003560.tar.gz. Vendor ticket created: VND-99871.
Sam: Copy of NVML excerpt for one card:
```
[2026-03-15T00:12:34Z] GPU0 Xid=31 CE count=184 soft_ecc=0.68% driver=nvdrv-2.14.3 kernel=6.2.15
[2026-03-15T00:12:37Z] PCIe reset issued to GPU0, unit lost for 3.4s
```
Ciara: Vendor responded preliminary — requesting kernel dmesg + firmware version. They flagged known boot-time regression with nvdrv-2.14.x and certain BIOS combos.
Lee: Ok — proceed with rollback canary to nvdrv-2.13.9 on rck-18 at 02:00 UTC, single-rack scope, health check window 20m. If pass -> schedule rolling back rck-17/rck-19 over next 6h.
ops-oncall: I'll own the runbook and be on shift during the canary. Paging on-call infra and vendor contacts.
Mike: Finance notified of potential burst spend. I'll hold off activating if canary recovers >8% capacity.
Anya: Great. I'll update status page and notify product about possible degraded capacity for the next 6-12h. :eyes: :shipit:
Sam: Thanks team. Keep updates tight — post any regression signals to this thread.
Ciara: Will do — posting timeline and live checks once rollback kicks off.
infra-bot: Incident INC-AP-5421 severity escalated to P2. Next update expected at 2221007200 or sooner.
